title: Poisson & Count Regression
interviewAnswer: Poisson regression models count outcomes with a log link and assumes the conditional variance equals the conditional mean. Overdispersion often motivates negative-binomial or quasi-likelihood alternatives.
keyPoints: Predictions are nonnegative through log link.
why: Poisson & Count Regression appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Poisson regression models count outcomes with a log link and assumes the conditional variance equals the conditional mean. Overdispersion often motivates negative-binomial or quasi-likelihood alternatives. Check overdispersion. Predictions are nonnegative through log link. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Model support-ticket counts per customer-month with log(exposure time) as an offset.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Poisson & Count Regression make?
How would you validate or debug Poisson & Count Regression in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
